blog:2.hook: Most Power BI training teaches the buttons, not the data model your leadership team numbers rest on.
blog:2.body: Power BI training usually walks through menus and charts. The hard part is the data model underneath: which tables connect, what each measure means, and who owns it. A two-day session on your own reports teaches more than a week of generic screenshots, because the model is where a wrong number starts.

linkedin:0.hook: If nobody can name who owns your revenue KPI, leadership is trusting a guess.
linkedin:0.body:
If your monthly numbers never quite reconcile between two teams, this is usually the reason, and it is worth a minute to explain.

The formula is almost always correct. The disagreement starts because two teams each decided what the number includes, and both wrote a correct formula for a different definition. Sales counts a signed order. Finance counts an invoiced one. Both are right, and the two reports disagree every month. A KPI definition on one page (name, formula, source, and owner) settles it for good.
linkedin:0.close: Which number in your company do two teams define two different ways?

linkedin:1.hook: Wenn niemand die Bedeutung einer KPI aufschreibt, ist die Zahl im Management am Ende geraten.
linkedin:1.body:
Kurz vorab, warum das mehr ist als Wortklauberei: eine Kennzahl ohne Besitzer wird in jedem Meeting neu ausgelegt.

In fast jedem Review stimmt die Formel. Es fehlt eine geschriebene Definition und ein Besitzer. Der Umsatz wird brutto, netto oder nach Lieferdatum gerechnet, und alle drei Zahlen sind fuer sich richtig. In Deutschland ist eine falsche Zahl im Management am Ende eine Haftungsfrage.

x:0.hook: A KPI is a number with a target and an owner. Without the owner, the KPI definition drifts.
x:0.body: Everyone writes the formula. Almost no one writes the KPI definition: what the number includes, and who decides the edge cases. That gap is why two dashboards show two different revenues for the same month.

beats.spoken: You are probably over-studying the Microsoft Certified Power BI Data Analyst Associate exam. It rewards three skills.
beats.screen: PL-300: the 3 skills that pass it
beats.prod: Talking head, tight. Cut on 'half the study'.

beats.spoken: One, Power Query. Learn how to unpivot a wide table into rows. It comes up on almost every exam, and it is two clicks once you have seen it.
beats.screen: 1. Power Query: unpivot a wide table
beats.prod: Screen-rec: select columns, right-click, Unpivot. Slow enough to copy.

beats.spoken: Two, DAX filter context. Just understand why one measure changes when you click a slicer. That single idea explains most of the DAX questions.
beats.screen: 2. DAX: why a measure changes with a slicer
beats.prod: Screen-rec: click a slicer, watch the number change. Zoom in.

beats.spoken: Three, build one clean report page on a real dataset. One good page teaches more than ten half-finished ones.
beats.prod: Show a single tidy report page.

beats.spoken: That is the whole plan, and it is free. Follow for a filter-context example you can copy next.
beats.prod: Back to talking head. One line.

shortform:3.hook: Most Power BI course tutorial videos teach you to build a wrong number quickly. Do these three steps first.

beats.spoken: Most Power BI course tutorial videos teach you to build a wrong number quickly. Do these three steps first.
beats.screen: POWER BI COURSE: do this before any chart
beats.prod: Talking head. Cut on 'come out right'.

beats.spoken: One, in Power Query, delete the columns you will never use. A lighter model is faster and easier to trust.
beats.screen: 1. Delete columns you will not use
beats.prod: Screen-rec: multi-select columns, Remove. Slow and clear.

beats.spoken: Two, connect customers to orders on the customer ID. One clean relationship, not a copy of the data in each table.
beats.screen: 2. One relationship on the customer ID
beats.prod: Screen-rec: drag the field, one line between two tables.

beats.spoken: Three, write one measure, total sales, and check it against a number you already trust. If it matches, the model is sound.
beats.screen: 3. Check one measure against a known number
beats.prod: Type the measure, compare to a known figure.

beats.spoken: That is the whole foundation, free. Follow for the first charts built on top of it.
